How the children imply the selected statement (this is the supplied proof):
1. Assume b ≠ −a. Then a ≠ b, because m(a) > 0 > m(b).
2. chord gives ℓ, u, b + ℓu = a, |b+su| ≤ 1 on [0, ℓ], and the meeting property.
3. Put mi := m − [·=a] + [·=b]. Applying competitor to Submission.idtp_fons_odc_polygonal_current, F, mo = m, mi, b, u, ℓ gives an integer multiplicity X with X(ω) = Σ m(e)∫_{(1,∞)} + Σ mi(e)∫_{(0,1)} + ∫_{(0,ℓ)}ω(b+su)[u], and M_{B_2}(X) ≤ Σ|m| + Σ|mi| + ℓ.
4. ray_split and the hypothesis on C give (X − C)(ω) = −∫_{(0,1)}ω(ta)[a] + ∫_{(0,1)}ω(tb)[b] + ∫_{(0,ℓ)}ω(b+su)[u].
5. ftc on the three segments, using b + ℓu = a, gives (X − C)(dφ) = 0, i.e. SameBoundary X C.
6. These integrands vanish when ω vanishes on closedBall(0,1). So support with U = ℝ^P and K = closedBall(0,1) gives spt(X − C) ⊆ closedBall(0,1) ⊆ B_2(0), and spt(X − C) is compact.
7. IsMinimizingIn C univ with W = B_2(0), where CompactlyContained W univ holds, gives M_W(C) ≤ M_W(X).
8. ray_current_rep gives R for C, and ray_mass with r = 2 gives M_W(C) = 2Σ|m|.
9. Since m(a) ≥ 1 and m(b) ≤ −1, Σ|mi| = Σ|m| − 2. Hence 2Σ|m| ≤ 2Σ|m| − 2 + ℓ, so ℓ ≥ 2.
10. The parallelogram law gives |a+b|² = 4 − ℓ² ≤ 0, so b = −a, a contradiction.

subproblems.title: The chord between two distinct, non-antipodal unit vectors stays in the closed unit ball and meets every line through 0 at most once (parent steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let a, b ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with |a| = |b| = 1, a ≠ b and b ≠ −a. Then there are ℓ ∈ ℝ and u ∈ ℝ^P such that ℓ > 0, |a − b| = ℓ, |u| = 1, b + ℓu = a, |b + su| ≤ 1 for every s ∈ [0, ℓ], and, for every e ∈ ℝ^P and s₁, s₂, t₁, t₂ ∈ ℝ, b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e imply s₁ = s₂ (the line s ↦ b + su meets each line ℝe through 0 in at most one parameter).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a b : Euclid P), ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖b‖ = 1 → a ≠ b → b ≠ -a → ∃ (ℓ : ℝ) (u : Euclid P), 0 < ℓ ∧ ‖a - b‖ = ℓ ∧ ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ b + ℓ • u = a ∧ (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) ℓ, ‖b + s • u‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ (e : Euclid P) (s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ), b + s₁ • u = t₁ • e → b + s₂ • u = t₂ • e → s₁ = s₂
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 1–2 (the chord [[b, a]] of the pairing argument), Simon 7.3.3, proof of (2), formula (10) (chapter-07.txt lines 563–566: "it is easy to check that such a 1-dimensional minimizing cone necessarily has the form m[[ℓ]]").
1. (Choice of ℓ and u.) Put ℓ := |a − b| and u := ℓ⁻¹(a − b). Since a ≠ b we have a − b ≠ 0, hence ℓ > 0 (norm_pos_iff), and |a − b| = ℓ holds by definition.
2. (Unit direction, endpoint.) |u| = |ℓ⁻¹|·|a − b| = ℓ⁻¹ℓ = 1 (norm_smul, ℓ > 0), and b + ℓu = b + (ℓℓ⁻¹)(a − b) = b + (a − b) = a.
3. (The chord lies in the closed unit ball.) Let s ∈ [0, ℓ] and put λ := s/ℓ; then 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1 because 0 ≤ s ≤ ℓ and ℓ > 0. By the definition of u, b + su = b + λ(a − b) = (1 − λ)b + λa. By the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the norm, |b + su| ≤ |1 − λ|·|b| + |λ|·|a| = (1 − λ) + λ = 1, using 1 − λ ≥ 0, λ ≥ 0 and |a| = |b| = 1.
4. (a and b are not on a common line through 0.) Suppose a, b ∈ span{e} for some e ∈ ℝ^P, say a = αe and b = βe with α, β ∈ ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_singleton). Then |α|·|e| = |a| = 1 and |β|·|e| = |b| = 1. In particular |e| ≠ 0 (otherwise 0 = 1), so cancelling |e| gives |α| = |β|, i.e. α = β or α = −β. If α = β then a = b; if α = −β then b = βe = −αe = −a. Both contradict the hypotheses a ≠ b and b ≠ −a.
5. (At most one meeting parameter.) Let e ∈ ℝ^P and s₁, s₂, t₁, t₂ ∈ ℝ with b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e, and suppose s₁ ≠ s₂. Subtracting the two equations, (s₁ − s₂)u = (t₁ − t₂)e ∈ span{e}; since s₁ − s₂ ≠ 0, u ∈ span{e} (Submodule.smul_mem_iff). Then b = t₁e − s₁u ∈ span{e} and, by step 2, a = b + ℓu ∈ span{e}. This contradicts step 4. Hence s₁ = s₂.
6. (Conclusion.) ℓ and u of step 1 satisfy ℓ > 0 and |a − b| = ℓ (step 1), |u| = 1 and b + ℓu = a (step 2), |b + su| ≤ 1 for all s ∈ [0, ℓ] (step 3) and the uniqueness property of step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: ℓ := |a − b| > 0 and u := ℓ⁻¹(a − b) give |u| = 1 and b + ℓu = a.
For s ∈ [0, ℓ], b + su = (1 − s/ℓ)b + (s/ℓ)a is a convex combination of unit vectors, so |b + su| ≤ 1.
Unit vectors a, b on a common line ℝe would satisfy a = ±b, which is excluded.
Two meeting points with s₁ ≠ s₂ would put u, then b and a = b + ℓu, into span{e}; hence s₁ = s₂.

subproblems.title: Splitting the ray integral of a test 1-form at t = 1 (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P) be a test 1-form on ℝ^P (TestFormOn univ 1: C^∞ with compact support) and let e ∈ ℝ^P with |e| = 1. Then ∫_{(0,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt = ∫_{(0,1)} ω(te)(e) dt + ∫_{(1,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt, where ω(x)(e) denotes the value of the 1-covector ω(x) on the 1-tuple (e) (fun _ => e) and the integrals are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals over the indicated subsets of ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (e : Euclid P), ‖e‖ = 1 → ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e) = (∫ t in Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) + ∫ t in Ioi (1 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 ("∫_{(0,∞)} ω(te)[e] dt = ∫_{(0,1)} + ∫_{(1,∞)} (the integrand is continuous with compact support along the isometric line, and {1} is null)").
Notation: γ(t) := te for t ∈ ℝ and f(t) := ω(γ(t))(e) = ω(te)(fun _ => e).
1. (γ is a closed embedding.) For x, y ∈ ℝ, |γ(x) − γ(y)| = |(x − y)e| = |x − y|·|e| = |x − y|, so γ is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq). An isometry from the complete space ℝ is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding).
2. (Continuity.) ω is a test form, so IsTestForm ω = IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω; in particular ω is C^∞ and hence continuous. The evaluation map ev_e : α ↦ α(fun _ => e) on 1-covectors is a continuous linear map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply). Hence f = ev_e ∘ ω ∘ γ is continuous.
3. (Compact support.) ω has compact support; composing with the closed embedding γ preserves compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding), so ω ∘ γ has compact support. Since ev_e(0) = 0, applying ev_e preserves compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). So f has compact support.
4. (Integrability.) A continuous function with compact support on ℝ is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport); hence f is integrable on every subset of ℝ (Integrable.integrableOn).
5. (Additivity.) (0, ∞) = (0, 1] ∪ (1, ∞) (Ioc_union_Ioi_eq_Ioi with 0 ≤ 1), the two pieces are disjoint (Ioc_disjoint_Ioi_same) and (1, ∞) is measurable, so by additivity of the set integral for integrable functions (setIntegral_union) ∫_{(0,∞)} f = ∫_{(0,1]} f + ∫_{(1,∞)} f.
6. (Removing the endpoint.) The singleton {1} is Lebesgue-null, so ∫_{(0,1]} f = ∫_{(0,1)} f (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo). Substituting into step 5 gives ∫_{(0,∞)} f = ∫_{(0,1)} f + ∫_{(1,∞)} f, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: t ↦ te is an isometry, hence a closed embedding of ℝ into ℝ^P.
t ↦ ω(te)(e) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable on every subset of ℝ.
(0,∞) = (0,1] ⊔ (1,∞) gives additivity of the integral, and {1} is null, so ∫_{(0,1]} = ∫_{(0,1)}.

subproblems.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus for a smooth 0-form along a segment
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let g be a C^∞ differential 0-form on ℝ^P (IsSmoothForm g). For every a, v ∈ ℝ^P and ℓ ≥ 0: ∫_{(0,ℓ)} (dg)(a + uv)(v) du = g(a + ℓv)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩. Here dg = exteriorDerivative g is a 1-form, (dg)(y)(v) is the value of the 1-covector dg(y) on the 1-tuple (v), and g(y)⟨⟩ is the value of the 0-covector g(y) on the empty tuple (fun i => i.elim0). The integral is the Lebesgue (Bochner) integral over the open interval (0, ℓ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0), IsSmoothForm g → ∀ (a v : Euclid P) (ℓ : ℝ), 0 ≤ ℓ → ∫ u in Ioo 0 ℓ, exteriorDerivative g (a + u • v) (fun _ => v) = g (a + ℓ • v) (fun i => i.elim0) - g a (fun i => i.elim0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted theorem: DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.closure_compact-a1.segment_current-a1.zero_form_ftc-a1 (status accepted, candidate 9e35a3d5, isolated comparator passed), with byte-identical frozen type; its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim below ("parent proof" there refers to that node's own parent). Role in the selected proof: step 5, applied to g = φ for a test 0-form φ (so IsSmoothForm g) along the segments t ↦ 0 + ta and t ↦ 0 + tb (ℓ = 1) and s ↦ b + su (length ℓ, ending at b + ℓu = a).
Source: parent proof step 8; Simon Ch. 6, 2.3 (chapter-06.txt lines 214–218: ∂T(ω) = T(dω)), which is motivated by Stokes' theorem (lines 210–213). In dimension one Stokes' theorem is the fundamental theorem of calculus.
Notation: ⟨⟩ := (fun i => i.elim0), the unique tuple Fin 0 → ℝ^P; ĝ(y) := g(y)⟨⟩ ∈ ℝ.
1. Smoothness of ĝ. ĝ = ev ∘ g, where ev := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ ℝ^P ℝ ⟨⟩ (α ↦ α⟨⟩) is a continuous linear map. A continuous linear map composed with the C^∞ map g is C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.comp). In particular ĝ is C¹ and differentiable everywhere, and y ↦ Dĝ(y) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Also g itself is differentiable (ContDiff.differentiable, since the smoothness order ∞ ≠ 0).
2. Value of dg on a 1-tuple. Since g is differentiable at y, exteriorDerivative_apply (= extDeriv_apply) gives, for w : Fin 1 → ℝ^P,
   dg(y)(w) = Σ_{i : Fin 1} (−1)^i · D(z ↦ g(z)(Fin.removeNth i w))(y)(w i) = D(z ↦ g(z)(Fin.removeNth 0 w))(y)(w 0),
   using Fin.sum_univ_succ and (−1)^0 = 1. For w = (fun _ => v), Fin.removeNth 0 w is a map Fin 0 → ℝ^P, so it equals ⟨⟩ (the type Fin 0 → ℝ^P is a subsingleton). Hence dg(y)(v) = Dĝ(y)v for every y ∈ ℝ^P.
3. Chain rule. For each u ∈ ℝ, the map u ↦ a + uv has derivative v at u (hasDerivAt_id, HasDerivAt.smul_const, HasDerivAt.const_add). ĝ has Fréchet derivative Dĝ(a + uv) at a + uv (step 1). So u ↦ ĝ(a + uv) has derivative Dĝ(a + uv)v at u (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt).
4. Integrability. u ↦ Dĝ(a + uv)v is continuous: it is the continuous map Dĝ (step 1), composed with the continuous u ↦ a + uv and evaluated at the fixed vector v. Hence it is interval integrable on [0, ℓ] (Continuous.intervalIntegrable).
5. Conclusion. Since ℓ ≥ 0 and singletons are Lebesgue-null, ∫_{(0,ℓ)} F du = ∫_{(0,ℓ]} F du = ∫_0^ℓ F du for every F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). Rewrite the integrand pointwise by step 2, then apply the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt with steps 3–4):
   ∫_{(0,ℓ)} dg(a + uv)(v) du = ∫_0^ℓ Dĝ(a + uv)v du = ĝ(a + ℓv) − ĝ(a + 0·v) = g(a + ℓv)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩. ∎
proof_key_steps: ĝ := g(·)⟨⟩ = ev_⟨⟩ ∘ g is C^∞, with continuous derivative.
extDeriv_apply on a 1-tuple: dg(y)(v) = Dĝ(y)v, because removeNth 0 of a 1-tuple is the empty tuple.
Chain rule: d/du ĝ(a + uv) = Dĝ(a + uv)v, which is continuous in u.
For ℓ ≥ 0, ∫ over (0,ℓ) equals the interval integral ∫_0^ℓ, and the FTC gives ĝ(a + ℓv) − ĝ(a).

subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) K → F ω = 0) → F.support ⊆ K ∧ IsCompact F.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted theorem: DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.constant_multiplicity_reduction-a1.support_of_vanishing-a1 (status accepted, candidate 02c6122c, isolated comparator passed), with byte-identical frozen type; its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim below ("parent proof" there refers to that node's own parent). Role in the selected proof: step 6, with U = ℝ^P, K = closedBall(0, 1) and F = X − C.
Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.

subproblems.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its representing measure, and its support is the support of that measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where H^n = μHE[n]). Write μ_R := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. Then: (a) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ U, where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum (in [0, ∞]) of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (b) for every x ∈ U: x ∈ spt T if and only if μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) every other representation R' of T has the same measure: R'.measure = R.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ (∀ x ∈ U, (x ∈ T.support ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → R.measure (ball x ε) ≠ 0)) ∧ ∀ R' : IMRep U n, R'.Represents T → R'.measure = R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted theorem: DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.im_mass_measure-a1 (status accepted, candidate 01ae2c59, isolated comparator passed), with byte-identical frozen type; it is also a resolved dependency of the selected node. Its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim below. Role in this split: part (a) with U = ℝ^P gives M_W(T) = R.measure(W) in the children ray_mass and competitor (step 8 of the selected proof).
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.8 and Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 224–300 and 733–775), which state these facts as evident; this is the identity "μ_S = R.measure for every representation R, M_W(S) = μ_S(W), spt S = spt μ_S" used throughout the parent proof (its Notation paragraph). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing multi-indices I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) (for n = 0, |α| = |α()|); dx^I is the dual basis covector.
1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)
2. (Consequences for R.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Hence, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Moreover β(x) := Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)·dx^I equals σ(x)·α_{τ(x)} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 there. The coefficients ξ(·)(dx^I) of β are H^n⌞M-measurable because ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); as μ_R ≪ H^n⌞M, β is μ_R-measurable.
3. (Radon property.) μ_R is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U) and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult). Since U is an open subset of ℝ^P, hence σ-compact, locally compact and second countable, the restriction of μ_R to U is a locally finite Borel measure on U and therefore outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on Borel subsets of U.
4. (Upper bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open and let ω be admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere). By R.Represents T and step 2, T(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_M θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n = μ_R(W), because ω vanishes off W. Taking ofReal and the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open, K ⊆ W compact and ε > 0. By step 3 choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and contained in W, and μ_R(V ∖ K) < ε. By Lusin's theorem (for the finite Radon measure μ_R⌞V and the μ_R-measurable map β of step 2, with values in the finite-dimensional space Λ^n of n-covectors) choose a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < ε and β|_{K'} continuous. Extend β|_{K'} to a continuous map ℝ^P → Λ^n (Tietze, coordinatewise) and compose with the retraction r(α) := α / max(1, |α|) (continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball) to obtain a continuous β̃ with |β̃| ≤ 1 and β̃ = β on K'. Take χ ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and put γ := χ·β̃ (continuous, |γ| ≤ 1, compact support in V). Let γ_j := γ * ϱ_{1/j} be the coordinatewise convolution with a standard mollifier. For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. So γ_j is admissible for M_W(T) and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(γ_j). By dominated convergence (dominating function θ·1_{closure V}, integrable by step 3), T(γ_j) = ∫_M θ·ξ(γ_j) dH^n → ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3ε for every compact K ⊆ W and every ε > 0, and inner regularity of μ_R on the open set W (step 3) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
6. ((b), "if".) Let x ∈ U with μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T). Then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, i.e. T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Every admissible value in the definition of M_W(T) is ofReal 0 = 0 (and the zero form is admissible), so M_W(T) = 0, and by (a) μ_R(W) = 0. For ε > 0 so small that B_ε(x) ⊆ W we get μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
7. ((b), "only if".) Let x ∈ spt T and suppose μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0. Choose ε' ∈ (0, ε) with closedBall x ε' ⊆ U (U is open). W := B_{ε'}(x) is open, its closure closedBall x ε' is compact and contained in U, and for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, step 2 gives |T(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ (sup_x |ω(x)|)·μ_R(W) = 0. So T vanishes on W, W belongs to the family defining zeroRegion(T), x ∈ zeroRegion(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T: a contradiction. Hence μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
8. ((c).) Let R' be another representation of T. By (a) applied to R and to R', R'.measure(W) = M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U. Both measures vanish on ℝ^P ∖ U (both carriers lie in U) and are finite on every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U (step 3). The open subsets of U with compact closure in U form a π-system (closed under finite intersections) generating the Borel σ-algebra of U (every open subset of U is a countable union of them), and U is the union of an increasing sequence of them on which both measures are finite. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for the unit simple orientation ξ(x), with equality for the dual covector β(x).
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) directly from the representation.
Lower bound by Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction to the unit ball, mollification and inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_R.
Support: T vanishes on W ⇔ M_W(T) = 0 ⇔ μ_R(W) = 0, giving spt T = spt μ_R inside U.
Representation independence: two representations agree on open subsets of U, hence (π-system uniqueness, σ-finiteness on U) everywhere.

subproblems.title: Mass of a weighted ray current in a ball centred at 0 (parent step 8, mass of C)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ 1), R an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ 1) with R.Represents C, F ⊆ ℝ^P a finite set of unit vectors and m : ℝ^P → ℤ such that R.measure(A) = Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|·ℒ¹((0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ A}) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for every r ∈ ℝ, M_{B_r(0)}(C) = C.massOn(B_r(0)) = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|)·r) in [0, ∞] (B_r(0) the open ball; both sides are 0 when r ≤ 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (F : Finset (Euclid P)), (∀ e ∈ F, ‖e‖ = 1) → ∀ m : Euclid P → ℤ, R.Represents C → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∑ e ∈ F, ENNReal.ofReal |(m e : ℝ)| * volume (Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∩ (fun t : ℝ => t • e) ⁻¹' A)) → ∀ r : ℝ, C.massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) r) = ENNReal.ofReal ((∑ e ∈ F, |(m e : ℝ)|) * r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 8 ("By ray_current_rep, C has a representation R_C with R_C.measure(A) = Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|·ℒ¹({t > 0 : te ∈ A}); by im_mass_measure (a) (with U = ℝ^P), M_W(C) = R_C.measure(W) ≥ Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|·ℒ¹((0, 2)) = 2Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|, since |te| = t < 2 for 0 < t < 2"); here the representation R is given and the same computation is carried out exactly for an arbitrary radius r.
1. (Mass equals representing measure.) ℝ^P is open and R represents C, so im_mass_measure (a) (dimred_im_mass_measure with U = ℝ^P, T = C) gives C.massOn(W) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. The open ball B_r(0) is open (also when r ≤ 0, where it is empty), hence C.massOn(B_r(0)) = R.measure(B_r(0)).
2. (Formula.) B_r(0) is Borel (measurableSet_ball), so by hypothesis R.measure(B_r(0)) = Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)| · ℒ¹((0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)}).
3. (The parameter set.) Let e ∈ F, so |e| = 1, and t ∈ ℝ. Then te ∈ B_r(0) ⟺ |te| < r ⟺ |t|·|e| < r ⟺ |t| < r. If t > 0 then |t| = t, so t ∈ (0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)} ⟺ 0 < t < r. Hence (0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)} = (0, r) (the empty set when r ≤ 0).
4. (Length.) ℒ¹((0, r)) = ofReal(r − 0) = ofReal(r) (Real.volume_Ioo; this equals 0 when r ≤ 0).
5. (Summation.) By steps 2–4, R.measure(B_r(0)) = Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)| · ofReal(r) = (Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)|) · ofReal(r) (Finset.sum_mul) = ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|) · ofReal(r) (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, each |m(e)| ≥ 0) = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|)·r) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, valid because Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)| ≥ 0). With step 1, C.massOn(B_r(0)) = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|)·r). ∎
proof_key_steps: im_mass_measure (a): C.massOn(B_r(0)) = R.measure(B_r(0)).
For a unit vector e, (0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)} = (0, r).
ℒ¹((0, r)) = ofReal r, and Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)|·ofReal r = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|)·r).

subproblems.title: The chord competitor: outer rays, inner segments and a chord form an integer multiplicity current with controlled mass in B_2(0) (parent step 3 and step 8, mass of X)
subproblems.statement: Assume (PC), the exact frozen statement of the sibling theorem idtp_fons_odc_polygonal_current: for every P ∈ ℕ, finite type ι, p, v : ι → ℝ^P with |v_k| = 1, open sets I_k ⊆ ℝ and c_k ∈ ℤ such that H¹(γ_j(I_j) ∩ closure(γ_k(I_k))) = 0 for all j ≠ k, where γ_k(t) := p_k + t·v_k and H¹ := μHE[1], there are X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) and an integer multiplicity triple R (IMRep univ 1) with R.Represents X, X(ω) = Σ_k c_k ∫_{I_k} ω(γ_k(t))(v_k) dt for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P), and R.measure(A) = Σ_k |c_k|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(A)) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then: for every P ∈ ℕ, every finite set F ⊆ ℝ^P of unit vectors, all mo, mi : ℝ^P → ℤ, b, u ∈ ℝ^P and ℓ ∈ ℝ with ℓ ≥ 0 and |u| = 1 such that the line s ↦ b + su meets every line through 0 in at most one parameter (for all e ∈ ℝ^P and s₁, s₂, t₁, t₂ ∈ ℝ, b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e imply s₁ = s₂), there is an integer multiplicity current X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (IsIntegerMultiplicity X) such that X(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} mo(e)·∫_{(1,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt + Σ_{e∈F} mi(e)·∫_{(0,1)} ω(te)(e) dt + ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(b + su)(u) ds for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P), and M_{B_2(0)}(X) = X.massOn(B_2(0)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)| + Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)| + ℓ).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (p v : ι → Euclid P) (I : ι → Set ℝ) (c : ι → ℤ), (∀ k, ‖v k‖ = 1) → (∀ k, IsOpen (I k)) → (∀ j k, j ≠ k → (μHE[1] : Measure (Euclid P)) (((fun t : ℝ => p j + t • v j) '' I j) ∩ closure ((fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) '' I k)) = 0) → ∃ (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1), R.Represents X ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, X ω = ∑ k, (c k : ℝ) * ∫ t in I k, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (p k + t • v k) (fun _ => v k)) ∧ ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∑ k, ENNReal.ofReal |(c k : ℝ)| * volume (I k ∩ (fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) ⁻¹' A)) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (F : Finset (Euclid P)), (∀ e ∈ F, ‖e‖ = 1) → ∀ (mo mi : Euclid P → ℤ) (b u : Euclid P) (ℓ : ℝ), 0 ≤ ℓ → ‖u‖ = 1 → (∀ (e : Euclid P) (s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ), b + s₁ • u = t₁ • e → b + s₂ • u = t₂ • e → s₁ = s₂) → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, IsIntegerMultiplicity X ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, X ω = ∑ e ∈ F, (mo e : ℝ) * (∫ t in Ioi (1 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) + ∑ e ∈ F, (mi e : ℝ) * (∫ t in Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) + ∫ s in Ioo (0 : ℝ) ℓ, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (b + s • u) (fun _ => u)) ∧ X.massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∑ e ∈ F, |(mo e : ℝ)| + ∑ e ∈ F, |(mi e : ℝ)| + ℓ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3 (the competitor X built by polygonal_current from outer rays, inner segments and the chord, with the overlap analysis) and step 8 (M_W(X) = R_X.measure(W) ≤ Σ_e |m(e)|·ℒ¹((1, 2)) + Σ_e |mi(e)|·ℒ¹((0, 1)) + ℒ¹((0, ℓ)), "because t > 1 and |te| < 2 force t ∈ (1, 2)"), stated for arbitrary multiplicities mo (outer rays) and mi (inner segments). The sibling polygonal_current enters as the hypothesis (PC), with its exact frozen type.
Notation: H¹ := μHE[1]; for p, w ∈ ℝ^P, γ_{p,w}(t) := p + tw (t ∈ ℝ); ω(x)(w) := ω(x)(fun _ => w).
1. (Subsingletons are H¹-null.) μHE[1] = c·μH[1] for a constant c ∈ [0, ∞) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), and the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure μH[1] has no atoms, i.e. μH[1]({x}) = 0 for every x, because 1 > 0 (Measure.nullSingletonClass_hausdorff). Hence H¹({x}) = c·0 = 0, and H¹(∅) = 0. So every set with at most one point is H¹-null. (This is also the line_param computation H¹({x}) = ℒ¹({0}) = 0 of the parent proof; the library fact is used so that no unaccepted sibling is needed.)
2. (Unit-speed lines.) If |w| = 1 then |γ_{p,w}(x) − γ_{p,w}(y)| = |(x − y)w| = |x − y|, so γ_{p,w} is an isometry ℝ → ℝ^P, hence a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), and therefore closure(γ_{p,w}(I)) = γ_{p,w}(closure I) for every I ⊆ ℝ (IsClosedEmbedding.closure_image_eq).
3. (Two ray pieces.) Let e, e' be unit vectors and A ⊆ (0, ∞), B ⊆ [0, ∞) such that A ∩ B = ∅ whenever e = e'. Then γ_{0,e}(A) ∩ γ_{0,e'}(B) is empty, in particular a subsingleton. Indeed, let te = se' with t ∈ A and s ∈ B. Taking norms, t = |t|·|e| = |s|·|e'| = s (t > 0, s ≥ 0). Then te = te' with t ≠ 0 gives e = e' (cancel t). So t ∈ A ∩ B, which is empty because e = e' — a contradiction.
4. (Chord against a line through 0.) For every e ∈ ℝ^P and all A, B ⊆ ℝ, γ_{b,u}(A) ∩ γ_{0,e}(B) is a subsingleton: two of its points have the form b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e, so s₁ = s₂ by the hypothesis on b and u, and the two points coincide.
5. (The configuration.) Let ι := F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit, a finite type (F also denotes the finite subtype of its elements). Define (p_k, v_k, I_k, c_k) by: for e in the first copy of F (outer rays) (0, e, (1, ∞), mo(e)); for e in the second copy of F (inner segments) (0, e, (0, 1), mi(e)); for the Unit index (the chord) (b, u, (0, ℓ), 1). Every v_k is a unit vector (elements of F, and u) and every I_k is an open interval.
6. (Overlap hypothesis of (PC).) Let j ≠ k. By step 2, γ_j(I_j) ∩ closure(γ_k(I_k)) = γ_j(I_j) ∩ γ_k(closure I_k), and by step 1 it suffices that this set is a subsingleton. Recall closure((1, ∞)) = [1, ∞) and closure((0, 1)) = [0, 1] (closure_Ioi, closure_Ioo), both contained in [0, ∞); (1, ∞) and (0, 1) are contained in (0, ∞); (1, ∞) ∩ [0, 1] = ∅ and (0, 1) ∩ [1, ∞) = ∅. The nine cases:
 (a) outer e, outer e': j ≠ k forces e ≠ e' (as elements of F, hence as vectors), so step 3 applies with A = (1, ∞), B = [1, ∞) (the disjointness requirement is vacuous).
 (b) outer e, inner e': step 3 with A = (1, ∞), B = [0, 1], which are disjoint.
 (c) outer e, chord: commute the intersection and apply step 4.
 (d) inner e, outer e': step 3 with A = (0, 1), B = [1, ∞), which are disjoint.
 (e) inner e, inner e': j ≠ k forces e ≠ e', so step 3 applies with A = (0, 1), B = [0, 1].
 (f) inner e, chord: commute and apply step 4.
 (g) chord, outer e' and (h) chord, inner e': step 4 directly.
 (i) chord, chord: excluded by j ≠ k.
7. (Apply (PC).) (PC) with P, ι, p, v, I, c gives X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) and R with R.Represents X — hence IsIntegerMultiplicity X — together with X(ω) = Σ_{k∈ι} c_k ∫_{I_k} ω(p_k + t v_k)(v_k) dt for every ω and R.measure(A) = Σ_{k∈ι} ofReal|c_k|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(A)) for every Borel A.
8. (The formula for X.) Split the sum over ι = F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit into the sum over the first copy of F, the sum over the second copy and the single chord term (Fintype.sum_sum_type, Fintype.sum_unique); use 0 + te = te on the ray pieces and c = 1 on the chord; and rewrite sums over the subtype F as Finset sums over F (Finset.sum_coe_sort). This gives X(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} mo(e)∫_{(1,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt + Σ_{e∈F} mi(e)∫_{(0,1)} ω(te)(e) dt + ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(b + su)(u) ds.
9. (Mass in B_2(0).) By im_mass_measure (a) (dimred_im_mass_measure with U = ℝ^P) for the open ball W = B_2(0), X.massOn(B_2(0)) = R.measure(B_2(0)) = Σ_{k∈ι} ofReal|c_k|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(B_2(0))). Estimate each term by monotonicity of ℒ¹: for an outer ray e, a parameter t ∈ (1, ∞) with |te| = |t| < 2 satisfies t ∈ (1, 2), so the term is ≤ ofReal|mo(e)|·ℒ¹((1, 2)); for an inner segment the parameter set is contained in (0, 1), so the term is ≤ ofReal|mi(e)|·ℒ¹((0, 1)); for the chord the parameter set is contained in (0, ℓ) and |c| = 1, so the term is ≤ ℒ¹((0, ℓ)). Since ℒ¹((1, 2)) = ofReal 1, ℒ¹((0, 1)) = ofReal 1 and ℒ¹((0, ℓ)) = ofReal ℓ (Real.volume_Ioo), and Σ ofReal|x_i|·ofReal L = ofReal((Σ|x_i|)·L) for L ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, ENNReal.ofReal_mul), the total is ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)|) + ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)|) + ofReal(ℓ) = ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)| + Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)| + ℓ) (ENNReal.ofReal_add; all three summands are ≥ 0, using ℓ ≥ 0). Hence X.massOn(B_2(0)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)| + Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)| + ℓ).
10. X from step 7 is integer multiplicity, satisfies the formula of step 8 and the mass bound of step 9. ∎
proof_key_steps: Subsingletons are H¹-null (μHE[1] is a multiple of the atomless μH[1]) and unit-speed lines are closed isometric embeddings, so closure(γ(I)) = γ(closure I).
Ray pieces from 0 with parameter sets in (0,∞) and [0,∞) can meet only for equal directions and a common parameter; the chord meets every line through 0 at most once.
All nine overlap cases of the configuration (outer rays (1,∞)e, inner segments (0,1)e, chord b + (0,ℓ)u) on F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit are H¹-null, so (PC) yields X and a representation R.
Regrouping the sum over F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit gives the formula for X; R.Represents X gives IsIntegerMultiplicity X.
im_mass_measure (a) and monotonicity of ℒ¹ bound M_{B_2(0)}(X) = R.measure(B_2(0)) by Σ|mo| + Σ|mi| + ℓ.
